newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FULL TEXT - GLAVERBEL EARNINGS STATEMENT.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - GLAVERBEL EARNINGS STATEMENT.

text.p: Following is the full text of
a statement on first-half 1996 released by Belgian glass
producer Glaverbel.
Glaverbel Group half-yearly results:
Standing up well to the economic downturn
The Glaverbel Group finished the first six months of 1996
with operating results down on those for the first half of 1995,
despite a recovery begun in the course of the last two months.
After the downturn in the economy - the worst in recent
years - sent glass prices crashing to a historic low, the close
of the first semester 1996 benefited from catching-up movements
in the construction and automotive sectors, with prices starting
to recover.
As for the Group's net results, these have remained at more
or less the same level as in the corresponding period last year,
thanks to a reduction in financial expenditure occasioned by:
- an improvement in the Group's financial structure, achieved
mainly through the capital increase carried out by the parent
company Glaverbel in July 1995, the sell-off of the glass bead
activities in December 1995, and the preference stock repaid by
AFG Industries in December 1995;
- the general fall in interest rates, to which the Group is
particularly sensitive.
CONSOLIDATED FIGURES (BEF million)
1996 1st half 1995 1st half
Gross operating cash flow(1) 3,060 3,590
Operating income 1,005 1,557
Current gross income (2) 392 550
Net income after taxes 298 366
Net income, Group share 227 261
(1) Operating income, plus depreciation, write-downs of assets
and provisions for operating risks and charges.
(2) Income before taxes, extraordinary income or charges,
including the income from companies consolidated by the equity
method.
Compared with the first half of 1995, the main changes in
the consolidation perimeter are the demerger of the glass bead
activities and the acquisition of IVB (F), which processes glass
for the construction sector, and of AST (B), which produces
automotive windscreens. The latter acquisition will not have any
effect on the consolidated sales figure, since its sales were
previously included in those of Splintex.
The consolidated sales come to BEF 18,342 million at the end
of June 1996, down 4% on the same period last year (down 1% for
the same consolidation perimeter). The weak demand and falling
prices both weighed on the sales growth. Note however that sales
were down by as much as 8% at the end of March 1996.
The consolidated gross operating cash flow stands at BEF
3,060 million, down 15% on last year (down 12% for the same
consolidation perimeter).
The consolidated operating result comes to BEF 1,005
million, lower than the previous year by BEF 552 million,
reflecting the drop in volumes and prices in the first months of
the year. However, this has been partly offset by cost-cutting
programmes, resulting in large productivity gains by production
units, both in central and in western Europe.
The current gross result is BEF 392 million.
The net financial expenditure (excluding dividends and
amortisation of goodwill) has improved significantly, falling
from BEF 1,134 million at the end of June 1995 to BEF 694
million at the close of the first half of 1996, thanks to the
reduction in the Group's debt burden.
The consolidated net result after taxes comes to BEF 298
million, compared with BEF 366 million during the corresponding
period in 1995, a decrease of 19%.
Comments on the results
In Europe, although nearly all of the Group's activities
were hit by the contraction in the market, in terms of both
volumes and prices, the same activities nevertheless managed to
safeguard their positions thanks to massive investments that
have now become operational, together with ongoing
cost-reduction and productivity programmes.
The Group has taken advantage of the present overcapacity
situation to shut down a float glass furnace for repairs from
February to August 1996 at its Czech subsidiary Glavunion.
Although the shutdown has affected Glavunion's results this
semester, the repairs have helped to trim the Group's capacity
at just the right time.
AFG Industries
With demand weakening and prices under pressure, AFG
Industries experienced a slight contraction in its results,
reducing its contribution to the Group's results by a small
amount.
Glaverbel's liquidation of its entire stake in AFG
Industries, announced in June last year, was realised on 14
August 1996. This has swelled the treasury by some BEF 7.2
billion, mainly generated by the sale of the credit received
from Asahi in part payment of the price. The arrangements for
the acquisition of the Glaverbel shares exchanged as part of
this transaction left the Group holding 678,088 of these shares,
representing 10% of the shares issued at a unit price of BEF
3,095, with a face value of some BEF 2.1 billion.
This transfer will appear in the accounts for the second
half-year, generating a net capital gain of the order of BEF 1.1
billion after deduction of the costs of raising loans that will
lower the average cost of the debt.
Prospects for the second half of 1996
The recovery begun at the end of the first six months is
pushing demand back up on the construction and automotive
markets in several European countries, and new price rises are
being signalled. And with one of its float line coming back on
stream at double capacity, Glavunion's contribution to the Group
results should be boosted, all the more so that it is now fully
controlled by the Group (the balance of the Glavunion shares was
acquired at the beginning of September 1996).
Added to the effects of the improved financial structure,
the Group's operational performance should lead to
second-semester profits (extraordinary items not included)
higher than those of the first six months.
Interim dividend
In view of the prospects for the second half of 1996, the
Board of Directors has decided to pay out a gross interim
dividend of BEF 28, payable in cash as of 2 December 1996. For
ordinary shares without VVPR strip, the net interim dividend
will amount to BEF 21 after deduction of 25% withholding tax.
For ordinary shares with VVPR strip, the net interim dividend
will amount to BEF 23.80 after deduction of 15% withholding tax.
We have reviewed the interim consolidation accounts of the
Glaverbel Group as of June 30, 1996 in accordance with the
relevant recommendation of the Institute of Company Auditors.
Our review consisted principally of analysis, comparison and
discussion of the half-yearly financial and accounting
information provided to us and, accordingly, was less extensive
in scope than an audit of the annual accounts the purpose of
which is to give an opinion on the true and fair view of the
Group's consolidated net worth, financial position and results
of operations at the end of the accounting year.
Our review did not reveal any matters which lead us to
believe that any significant adjustment is required to the
interim consolidated accounts taking account of the company's
accounting principles.
Price Waterhouse Company Auditors SCC
Represented by Paul Pauwels and Martin Clayton
September 11, 1996
